nodes.label: Cleanup Issue 05: One Comparison Accessor
nodes.rationale: Resolved: run_metric and run_field collapsed into one run_value accessor with 29 call sites updated across pr_comparison.py and scripts/run_pr_comparison.py, and a missing name still returns None. The comparison JSON, report, and model-card addendum regenerate byte-identical from the three committed run directories. A review fix replaced the COMPARISON_METRICS gate with block-membership dispatch so a metric resolves from the block it names and the accessor genuinely defaults to overall.

nodes.label: PR Sample Reconciliation and Definition of Done
nodes.norm_label: pr sample reconciliation and definition of done
nodes.rationale: Every count must reconcile before anything is published: feature table 1,808,013 rows / 253,421 positives; BP-valid 15+ 1,805,697 / 253,091; BP-valid 15-49 1,290,219 / 112,898; BP-valid 50+ 515,478 / 140,193. The 2,316 rows without a valid BP pair are excluded from the BP model but retained in the table and described in the audit. Additional done criteria are both PR runs with full artifacts, a comparison report covering sample/feature/overall/calibration/threshold/sex/age-band/subgroup tables, the model-card addendum, all tests passing, and no microdata or model binaries committed.

nodes.label: 32-Feature State-Free Primary Feature Policy
nodes.rationale: The deployed model uses 32 of the 35 model-input columns. state is excluded to reduce local access- and diagnosis-pattern leakage; religion and social_group are excluded because they are sensitive attributes. State, fairness, and combined variants (33/34/35 features) exist so the impact of those exclusions is measured rather than assumed. Identifiers, cluster/household/line, PSU, strata, weights, target components, age_15_49, and the raw sex/residence encodings are never inputs; female and urban are the binary encodings used. Nominal categoricals use LightGBM native handling, ordinal variables stay ordered integers, and validation raises on forbidden or missing columns.

nodes.label: Subgroup and Fairness Audit
nodes.rationale: Required subgroups are sex, age band, wealth quintile, residence, education, and state (with at least 500 test respondents); religion and social group are audit-only because they are not deployed features. Sex-specific metrics are mandatory because the pooled sample is roughly 88% female, and every row carries n, positives, and prevalence so small groups are not overinterpreted. Groups under 200 respondents or 50 positives are flagged unreliable and never used to claim fairness. The report states that removing a protected attribute does not make a model fair and that gaps are descriptive, not causal; this spec audits fairness and does not mitigate it.

nodes.norm_label: cleanup issue 02: cli guards for untested entry points
nodes.rationale: Resolved: the guards already existed, so the work was the missing tests. tests/test_run_primary_model_cli.py and tests/test_verify_pr_samples_cli.py follow the importlib-plus-main pattern, point at a nonexistent table under tmp_path, and assert exit 1, the missing path, the build command, no traceback, and nothing written, without training.

nodes.label: Cleanup Issue 03: One Config Assembler for Primary and PR Models
nodes.norm_label: cleanup issue 03: one config assembler for primary and pr models
nodes.rationale: Resolved. src/screener/_config_assembly.py holds assemble_config, shared_subgroups, the single AGE_15_49_BANDS/AGE_15_49_LABELS, and the metadata helper; primary_15_49_config and _pr_config supply only differences. PRIMARY_CATEGORICAL_FEATURES and the always-empty categorical computation were deleted with a test pinning categorical_columns == (), duplicated PRIMARY_AGE_* and PR_15_49_AGE_* constants were removed rather than aliased, and TrainingConfig.to_dict() is byte-identical for nine variants. A review fix made the assembler's shared settings required and renamed the helper to config_metadata to match the run_metadata.json artifact.

nodes.label: One Shared Config Assembly Path
nodes.rationale: The public config builders stay the interface; behind them one internal assembler builds the shared pipeline config shape (target columns and definition, cluster/household/weight columns, folds, test fraction, sensitivity, bootstrap, SHAP sample size, split assignment, smoke rows, metadata) while each family supplies only run name, feature columns, sample filters, age bands and labels, subgroup extras, role, and sample label. The shared subgroup set and the 15-49 bands/labels are declared once, and the primary config's always-empty categorical tuple and its backing constant are deleted so nothing suggests the deployed model can use state, religion, or social group.

nodes.label: Review Cleanup and Python 3.11 Rerun (spec)
nodes.rationale: A two-axis review of the ticket 07 work found the primary and PR paths share almost no code where they are meant to behave identically, the new CLIs had no tests, and the primary config computed a categorical-feature tuple that always yields nothing (suggesting the deployed model could use state, religion, or social group). The refactors collapse duplicated config, subgroup, reconciliation, and summary logic behind existing seams, merge the two comparison accessors, and add CLI guard tests, all behaviour-preserving: the only changed numbers should come from the rerun.

nodes.label: Issue 02: PR Split Reuse and Assignment
nodes.norm_label: issue 02: pr split reuse and assignment
nodes.rationale: Resolved. src/screener/splits.py became the shared split seam: assign_splits owns the cluster-grouped 20% holdout and 5-fold rule and assign_pr_splits accepts an optional primary assignment, reusing it per cluster and assigning PR-only clusters with the same seed and stratification; assignment_source records per-row provenance and the summary records split_source. The test phase fills the global holdout quota across strata so reused primary test clusters cannot drag the holdout away from 20%, and household identity is the (cluster, household) pair because DHS hv002 numbers repeat across clusters. Real PR-only run: 1,808,013 rows, 30,125 clusters, 361,364 test rows (19.99%), leakage checks pass; final validation rejects degenerate partitions and non-covering summaries.

nodes.label: Issue 03: PR 15+ BP Model Run
nodes.rationale: Resolved. Because the external primary-model-pipeline spec was not implemented, it was built first as the shared seam (pipeline.py with TrainingConfig/TrainingResult/run_training_pipeline, modeling.py, calibration.py, metrics.py, feature_policy.py, model_bundle.py) so the PR run reuses it instead of growing a second path. PR-specific work is configuration only in src/screener/pr_model.py: pr_15_plus_config sets the PR table, age >= 15, BP-valid filters, target, cluster grouping, household, weight_scaled, and PR subgroups, with the 12-feature default. scripts/run_pr_model.py adds --sample, --smoke, --bootstrap, --shap-sample, --no-split-assignment, --feature-variant; smoke samples after filtering so it never trains on the full table. A review pass fixed weighted prevalence, cluster-label alignment in the bootstrap, the ignored split_assignment_path, and missing report sections.

nodes.label: Issue 04: PR 15-49 Age-Matched Run
nodes.rationale: Resolved as configuration on the shared pipeline. pr_15_49_config adds a single SampleFilter on age_15_49 on top of the PR 15+ filters; the previous age <= 49 filter was removed so the configured sample cannot drift from build_pr_features. reconcile_pr_15_49_sample and pr_sample_summary share the flag definition, and the run loads the saved PR split assignment, filtering to its case_ids with no re-split. The CLI refuses --no-split-assignment for 15-49 because a fresh partition would confound the comparison; calibration and threshold come from the run's own out-of-fold predictions. Config metadata carries sample, run_role, and comparison_run.

nodes.label: Issue 05: PR Subgroups, Fairness, and Feature-Set Variants
nodes.norm_label: issue 05: pr subgroups, fairness, and feature-set variants
nodes.rationale: Resolved inside the shared pipeline seam. _subgroup_metrics emits n, positives, prevalence, ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, sensitivity, specificity, ECE, gaps versus overall, a reliable flag, an unreliable_reason, and the audit-only note; the 200-row/50-positive and 500-row state rules became small_group_min_rows, small_group_min_positives, and state_min_test_rows config fields. Religion and social group join the subgroup set only for fairness and combined variants so exclusion decisions are tested rather than assumed. Variant comparison is a pure helper in src/screener/pr_variants.py that reports added/removed features and deltas and does not treat higher ROC-AUC as proof a variant is better; scripts/run_pr_variants.py requires the saved split assignment.

nodes.label: Issue 06: Primary vs PR Comparison Report
nodes.norm_label: issue 06: primary vs pr comparison report
nodes.rationale: Resolved in src/screener/pr_comparison.py. compare_primary_vs_pr is pure over three finished TrainingResults and returns run snapshots, sample and feature tables, overall and weighted metric blocks, descriptive deltas, reliability curves, sex and age-band rows, PR subgroup gaps, narrative, and limitations. Missing metrics render as n/a rather than raising, so a partial run stays comparable without inventing values; composition is reported on the test set because that is the set every run's metrics use. load_run_result reconstructs a result from a finished run's artifacts, and the CLI writes both Markdown and JSON. A review pass moved the shared scalar formatters into reporting.py.

nodes.label: Issue 07: Real-Data PR Runs and Publishable Aggregate Outputs
nodes.norm_label: issue 07: real-data pr runs and publishable aggregate outputs
nodes.rationale: Resolved. A primary CLI (scripts/run_primary_model.py plus src/screener/primary_model.py) was written first as a thin wrapper so the comparison has a real reference run; the primary run generated the cluster partition and the PR partition was rebuilt with --primary-assignment, so both PR runs record split_source: mixed. Published: primary 15-49 774,861 rows / 64,526 positives, LightGBM isotonic, ROC-AUC 0.7099, PR-AUC 0.2035, threshold 0.0549, sensitivity 0.8096, specificity 0.4558; PR 15-49 1,290,219 / 112,898, ROC-AUC 0.6979, PR-AUC 0.1900; PR 15+ 1,805,697 / 253,091, ROC-AUC 0.7459, PR-AUC 0.3320. Sample reconciliation is a repeatable command (scripts/verify_pr_samples.py); split assignments, per-respondent SHAP values, bundles, and microdata stay gitignored. A post-review fix added config.relative_to_project so published run records hold project-relative paths.

nodes.label: Issue 08: PR Sensitivity Model-Card Addendum
nodes.rationale: Resolved. The addendum is generated, not hand-written: render_pr_model_card_addendum in src/screener/pr_comparison.py reads the comparison structure and write_primary_vs_pr_report writes pr_sensitivity_model_card_addendum.md beside the report, with a custom comparison stem keeping the back-link correct. Its tables use the ticket 07 runs' real values and the sample table is read from the comparison summary so counts cannot drift; the only hard-coded sample fact is that 183 transgender respondents were excluded. It claims no fairness-variant result and states that only aggregate counts, metrics, and run identifiers are published.

nodes.label: Primary vs PR Side-by-Side Comparison Report
nodes.norm_label: primary vs pr side-by-side comparison report
nodes.rationale: The report compares sample, feature set (32 vs 12), discrimination, calibration, threshold behaviour, sex and age-band metrics, and PR subgroup gaps across the primary, PR 15-49, and PR 15+ runs. It compares discrimination, calibration, and threshold behaviour rather than raw probability levels because samples and feature sets differ, and it must not claim one model is universally better. The PR 15-49 run isolates the feature-set trade-off while the PR 15+ run adds older adults; it is not a pure ablation because the instruments differ.

nodes.label: 12-Feature Default PR BP Set and Its Variants
nodes.norm_label: 12-feature default pr bp set and its variants
nodes.rationale: The default uses female, age, urban, wealth, education, tobacco_any, alcohol_any, systolic_mean, diastolic_mean, bp_readings, bp_high, and bp_medication. Anthropometry is excluded because it is measured only for younger women and men, which would make missingness age- and sex-dependent; state, religion, and social_group are excluded to match the primary model's portability and fairness policy; diet, marital status, children ever born, smoking/smokeless split, and alcohol frequency are absent from the PR file; cooking fuel is reserved for an optional household-SES variant. State, fairness, combined, and cooking-fuel variants test those exclusion decisions.

nodes.label: PR Sensitivity Model-Card Addendum
nodes.rationale: The addendum documents intended use, sample and feature differences, the age gradient, calibration, threshold, subgroup gaps, label bias, limitations, and non-goals so the analysis cannot be mistaken for the deployed screener or a clinical tool. It must state that PR religion and social group describe the household head, that 183 transgender respondents were excluded, and that the PR model uses neither anthropometry nor diet, while remaining publishable without microdata.

nodes.label: PR Split Reuse of the Primary Cluster Partition
nodes.norm_label: pr split reuse of the primary cluster partition
nodes.rationale: The PR runs inherit the primary cluster-grouped 20% holdout and 5-fold development CV; overlapping clusters reuse their primary split and fold and PR-only clusters are assigned deterministically with the same seed and stratification, so comparisons are not confounded by a different partition. The split source is recorded as reused_primary, pr_only, or mixed, and leakage assertions cover clusters and households. The 15-49 comparison is the same partition filtered, never re-split.

nodes.label: Three Baselines and Validation-Only Model Selection
nodes.norm_label: three baselines and validation-only model selection
nodes.rationale: Three models are required: a prevalence-only floor, a logistic regression with imputation/encoding/scaling and balanced weights, and LightGBM with native categoricals, missing-value support, class weighting, and early stopping. PR-AUC ranks on development CV and Brier/log loss break ties, because accuracy would reward the majority class and a well-ranked but poorly calibrated model is unacceptable for a screener. Tuning stays inside training folds and the test set is evaluated once after a refit on the full development set. Weighted training is a sensitivity analysis only, so probabilities stay individual-level.

nodes.label: Cluster-Grouped Split Strategy
nodes.rationale: The primary grouping unit is the cluster (PSU) because keeping clusters intact blocks both household and community leakage. A 20% cluster-grouped holdout is created first, the remaining 80% is developed with 5-fold cluster-grouped CV, splitting is stratified on target and sex where feasible, and the pipeline asserts no cluster or household crosses a split or fold. Household-grouped splitting stays available as a configurable sensitivity check. The test set is untouched until selection, calibration, and threshold tuning finish, so those steps cannot peek.

nodes.label: Deferred Scope: Ensembles, Deployment, PR BP Model
nodes.norm_label: deferred scope: ensembles, deployment, pr bp model
nodes.rationale: Out of scope: the PR 15+ BP sensitivity model and its PR feature builder (a separate spec), the questionnaire-only, deployed state-specific and combined models beyond sensitivity roles, a 5-fold x 10-seed ensemble, large-scale hyperparameter search, FastAPI/demo/Docker/deployment, external and clinical validation, causal inference, fairness mitigation, small-area estimates, ONNX/mobile export, and redistributing microdata. A single-seed 5-fold run is the required implementation; the remaining variants follow once the pipeline is proven.

nodes.label: Metrics and PSU-Clustered Bootstrap Intervals
nodes.rationale: Confidence intervals resample PSUs (default 1,000 replicates) so uncertainty reflects the survey design instead of pretending respondents are independent; small subgroups may use fewer replicates. Unweighted metrics are primary and survey-weighted metrics are a sensitivity analysis, so sample performance and population performance are distinguished. The weight is never treated as a sample-size multiplier, and all metrics are computed from calibrated probabilities.

nodes.label: End-to-End Integration Test at the Pipeline Seam
nodes.norm_label: end-to-end integration test at the pipeline seam
nodes.rationale: Tests assert externally observable behaviour - leakage-free splits, numerically correct metrics, in-range probabilities, a threshold that meets its sensitivity target on separable data, and a reloaded bundle reproducing predictions - rather than tree structures or column order. One integration test drives run_training_pipeline with a 300-500 row synthetic table and small config under about 60 seconds, while deterministic pure helpers (splits, metrics, calibration, threshold, subgroups, feature policy, artifact round-trip) are tested directly. No network, DVC, or GPU; real-data training is verified by manual smoke run.

nodes.label: Reproducibility, Python 3.11/3.12, and No Microdata Publication
nodes.norm_label: reproducibility, python 3.11/3.12, and no microdata publication
nodes.rationale: Seeds, resolved config, dataset fingerprint, row/column counts, prevalence, package versions, and git commit are recorded so a result can be traced and repeated. Modeling targets Python 3.11 or 3.12 because LightGBM and SHAP wheels may lag on 3.14 (a premise later corrected by the review-cleanup amendment). A small-sample smoke mode keeps the full pipeline exercisable, and raw/processed microdata and model binaries are never committed.

nodes.label: Sensitivity-First Screening Threshold (target 80%)
nodes.rationale: The screener rules people in for further testing, so the default operating point maximises specificity subject to at least 80% sensitivity, ties broken by PPV, and the target is configurable for clinics with different referral capacity. The threshold is selected on out-of-fold development predictions, never on the test set; 0.5 is reported only for reference, and sensitivity at 80% specificity is reported as a threshold-independent model comparison.

nodes.label: SHAP Global and Local Explanations
nodes.rationale: SHAP runs on a fixed 5,000-row test sample so the run stays tractable, and a local explanation function returns a single respondent's top contributing features with direction and impact for the future API. Explanations are described as associations, not causes. If SHAP is unavailable the pipeline falls back to permutation or native LightGBM gain importance and records the fallback.

nodes.label: Amendment: Python 3.11 Rerun Withdrawn
nodes.rationale: The 1 November 2026 amendment withdraws the rerun half and deletes ticket 06: the premise was wrong because every dependency ships a cp314 wheel, the CUDA and CatBoost GPU paths are verified, and the suite passes on 3.14.6, so the README now names 3.14.6. The rerun work belongs to model-shortlist tickets 05 and 06, which replace all three run directories under a new recipe; running this spec's rerun first would produce three full runs of the old recipe and then delete them. Tickets 02-05 carry forward, and 03/04 should land before model-shortlist 01/02 so the new families extend one config path.

nodes.label: PR 15+ BP-Based Sensitivity Model (spec)
nodes.rationale: The primary model is capped at 15-49 by the IR/MR recodes, yet adults 50+ in the PR file have 27.20% prevalence against 8.75% at 15-49, and the primary sample is about 88% female. The PR household-member file covers 1,808,013 adults 15+ with 99.87% BP coverage, so it supports a large-sample BP-based sensitivity analysis on the highest-prevalence age group. The PR model is deliberately a sensitivity analysis, never the deployed model, and it depends on the primary pipeline so there is one modeling implementation.

nodes.label: Primary Model Training and Evaluation (spec)
nodes.rationale: A naive random split would put household or cluster members on both sides and inflate performance, a single accuracy number would hide class imbalance and miscalibration, and no subgroup reporting would hide poor performance for men, older adults, or poorer households. So the pipeline must be leakage-free, baseline-compared, sensitivity-first, calibrated, and honestly reported as aggregate results plus a model bundle that can later be served without redistributing microdata.

nodes.label: Cleanup Issue 01: Shared Run Summary and Row-Count Accessor
nodes.norm_label: cleanup issue 01: shared run summary and row-count accessor
nodes.rationale: Resolved. build_run_summary builds the printed mapping and TrainingResult.row_counts is the single accessor the summary reads; both entry points call the shared function and no longer build the mapping inline. sample defaults to the pipeline's recorded label so the primary run does not duplicate the constant, while PR runs pass the CLI sample name and print the metadata label separately. Verified with 1,000-row smoke runs on both entry points: the PR JSON is identical except run_dir, and the primary JSON keeps every value and gains only sample_label and comparison_run, giving both the same shape and key order.

nodes.label: One Shared Run Summary Function
nodes.rationale: Both run entry points should print their end-of-run summary from one library function that takes the pipeline result plus the smoke flag, reconciliation status, and documented counts, so the primary and PR runs cannot drift in reported fields. It touches no filesystem and trains nothing, so it is unit-testable against a fake result in seconds. Row counts go through one accessor on the run result rather than repeated nested metadata lookups, so a metadata-shape change breaks one line.

nodes.label: Issue 01: PR Feature Table and Audit
nodes.norm_label: issue 01: pr feature table and audit
nodes.rationale: Resolved. build_pr_features was implemented in src/screener/features.py with pure helpers for code cleaning, sex-specific anthropometry, and cooking-fuel classification, plus build_pr_feature_audit, reconcile_pr_audit, and scripts/build_pr_features.py. nodes.label: Harmonised PR Feature Table
nodes.rationale: The table mirrors the IR/MR harmonised schema where a concept exists and keeps concepts the PR file lacks as explicit missing values rather than omitting them, so the same training and reporting code consumes it. It adds PR-specific cooking_fuel and cooking_fuel_clean, retains anthropometry where the PR file measures it so a future variant needs no rebuild, and reuses existing cleaning and target helpers. The builder validates required columns and codes and fails loudly. Expected size: 1,808,013 rows, 253,421 positives, 14.02%; 962,219 women and 845,794 men; 516,182 aged 50+ at 27.20% prevalence; 183 transgender respondents excluded because the audit sample and primary model use sex codes 1 and 2.

nodes.label: Cleanup Issue 04: One Reconciliation Rule, One Declaration per Count
nodes.norm_label: cleanup issue 04: one reconciliation rule, one declaration per count
nodes.rationale: Resolved. One private _compare_counts in features.py backs the PR feature-table audit, the PR BP-valid 15+ and 15-49 samples, and the primary 15-49 sample; a second helper _sample_reference names the narrowing the three sample reconcilers share. Returned shapes and key order are unchanged (reconcile_pr_audit stays {status, checks} with no summary) and each count is declared once in PRIMARY_REFERENCE, PR_REFERENCE_COUNTS, and PR_15_49_REFERENCE. Two reference-record assertions keep their literals deliberately as the pin on the documented values.

nodes.label: One Reconciliation Rule and One Declaration per Count
nodes.norm_label: one reconciliation rule and one declaration per count
nodes.rationale: All four reconcilers - PR feature-table audit, PR BP-valid 15+, PR BP-valid 15-49, and primary 15-49 - should delegate to one comparison helper while keeping the existing {status, summary, checks} shape so serialized run metadata does not change. Each documented count is declared once per sample, so a recount is a one-place edit rather than a hunt through constants, tests, and prose.

nodes.label: Out-of-Fold Isotonic vs Platt Calibration
nodes.rationale: Calibration is essential because the product displays probabilities: a predicted 20% risk must mean roughly 20%. Isotonic and Platt are both fitted on out-of-fold development predictions and the winner is chosen by Brier score and log loss rather than by convention. The report shows reliability curves before and after, slope, intercept, Brier, log loss, and ECE, unweighted and survey-weighted, and by wealth, sex, and state where subgroup sizes permit.

nodes.label: Run Artifacts and Schema-Validated Model Bundle
nodes.norm_label: run artifacts and schema-validated model bundle
nodes.rationale: Each run writes to a unique timestamp/seed/hash directory with split assignment, resolved config, metadata, metrics, subgroup metrics, calibration curve, threshold analysis, feature importance, SHAP data, report, model card, and bundle. The bundle carries the fitted model, calibrator, feature and categorical columns, threshold, target definition, sample metadata, versions, and run id, so inference cannot silently diverge from training. The bundle is local-only and gitignored while aggregate outputs are publishable; the loader validates the schema and does not reimplement preprocessing.
